solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Value a very quiet lift (8)

blocks.note: pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet

annotation.surface: Someone prizes a lift that runs almost silently.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Value' is a verb here, and 'lift' is a verb too, not the British word for an elevator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to appraise is to assess what something is worth.

entries.clue: Knowing chief, initially, ruler finally, in a word (4)

definitions.text: chief, initially, ruler finally, in a word

blocks.note: a sly, knowing look or remark

blocks.clueFragment: chief, initially, ruler finally, in a word
blocks.note: a word-part meaning chief at the front of words (archbishop) and ruler at the end (monarch)

annotation.surface: A riddle about a chief and a ruler, summed up in a word.
annotation.walkthrough: Really three meanings: 'initially' and 'finally' look like first-letter and last-letter instructions, but they say where in a word ARCH sits: arch- in front means chief, -arch at the end means ruler.
annotation.definitionFit: An arch smile or remark is knowing and mischievous.

entries.clue: Merchant of Venice, something that’s played up (4)

blocks.note: Marco, the thirteenth-century Venetian trader who travelled to China
a team game whose players ride horses, so it is played up in the saddle

annotation.surface: Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, and something performed on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Merchant of Venice' wants to be Shylock or Antonio from the play; it is Marco Polo. 'Up' is the rider's position, high on a horse.
annotation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was a Venetian merchant; polo is a game played mounted.

entries.clue: Metal that carries half the current in America (9)

indicators.note: the American word holds the extra letter inside it

blocks.note: the American name for the metal
I is the symbol for electric current; the full word has two of them, so ALUMINUM has half

annotation.surface: A metal wire that conducts part of the electric current in the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: Americans spell and say it ALUMINUM, with one I; the British spelling has two, so the US word carries half the currents.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the answer is the light silvery element used for cans and foil.

entries.clue: Orthodox playwright first to recognise resistance to rapid transit system? (5,7)

indicators.note: the first letter of 'recognise'

blocks.note: J M Barrie, author of Peter Pan

annotation.surface: A traditional dramatist is the first to spot opposition to a new metro line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rapid transit system' looks like an underground railway; the question mark admits it means anything moving fast through the air.
annotation.definitionFit: The sound barrier is the sharp rise in drag an aircraft meets near the speed of sound.

entries.clue: Inhabitant of one African state thus joined with another (6)

annotation.surface: Someone from one African country whose state has been merged with a neighbour.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a person from Somalia, built from a second country, Mali.
annotation.definitionFit: The answer is the word for a person from Somalia, on the Horn of Africa.

entries.clue: What may be added to cocktail? Nothing, as it happens (5)

definitions.text: What may be added to cocktail?

blocks.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens

annotation.surface: A barman's quiz: what goes in the cocktail? Nothing, as it turns out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As it happens' reads as 'incidentally'; it is the description of a live broadcast. The question mark flags that an olive is only one possible garnish.
annotation.definitionFit: An olive is the classic garnish dropped into a martini.

entries.clue: Counting everything wrong in eg her total he later got revised (10)

indicators.note: the letters of 'eg her total' are set wrong
the letters of 'he later got' are revised into a new order

blocks.note: a first anagram of the same ten letters, set 'wrong', which gives the answer on its own
second anagram fodder, the same 10 letters

annotation.surface: Someone totting up a sum finds the total wrong and has to revise it.
annotation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams of the same ten letters, each with its own indicator; either one alone would give the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Altogether means in total, with everything counted.

entries.clue: Not prepared to read statement of my intention to go through again (10)

blocks.note: I'll = I will, a statement of intent
to iterate is to repeat, go through again

annotation.surface: Someone refuses to read a statement and says they will go over it again instead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not prepared to read' sounds like unwillingness; it means not equipped to read at all.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Not prepared' in the sense of not equipped: someone who never learnt to read is in no position to.

entries.clue: Our request for communication about copper’s mathematical system (8)

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so CALL US goes round the outside of CU

blocks.note: 'call us', as a firm might ask
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

annotation.surface: A plea to get in touch about a police officer's maths.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is a British slang word for a police officer, which the possessive plays on; here it is the element.
annotation.definitionFit: Calculus is the branch of mathematics dealing with rates of change.

entries.clue: Mass reflected on sanctimonious saint’s piece (6)

indicators.note: LOT is turned back to front
in an across clue, the reversed part comes after what it is on

annotation.surface: A statue of a smug holy figure seems to reflect Mass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mass' with its capital looks like the church service; it is just a large amount. 'Piece' is slang for a gun.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'piece' is American slang for a gun, and the answer is a handgun.

entries.clue: For instance, workers in office breaking up (12)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing inside another, so EG MEN go inside STATION

blocks.note: one's station is one's post or office

annotation.surface: Staff in an office drifting apart, as a team breaks up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Office' here is a post or position, as in 'a station in life', not a room full of desks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: segmentation is the splitting of something into segments.

entries.clue: Intermediate delay, we hear, for pugnacious sportsman (12)

indicators.note: WAIT is heard, and spelt as WEIGHT

annotation.surface: A mid-length pause, apparently, in the case of a combative athlete.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pugnacious sportsman' is a fighter in the literal sense: a boxer.
annotation.definitionFit: A middleweight is a boxer in the weight class between welterweight and light heavyweight.

entries.clue: Wine in small measure of alcohol designed to avoid damage (10)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing inside another, so HOCK sits inside S before PROOF is added

blocks.note: proof measures a spirit's alcoholic strength

annotation.surface: Wine served in a small tot of spirit, made up so as to do no harm.
annotation.walkthrough: Hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine; proof is the scale of a spirit's strength.
annotation.definitionFit: Shockproof goods are built to withstand knocks without damage.

entries.clue: Like one part or another of minute without anxiety (10)

definitions.text: Like one part or another of minute

blocks.clueFragment: Like one part or another of minute
blocks.note: the word is said MIN-it (sixty seconds) or my-NEWT (tiny); either way one syllable carries no emphasis

annotation.surface: Relaxed about a tiny detail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as a unit of time; the clue means the written word, whose stress moves between its two syllables depending on the meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: An unstressed syllable carries no emphasis; an unstressed person is free of anxiety.

entries.clue: Capital including a reduced number in greeting (5)

indicators.note: 'including' means containing, so HI holds A NO between its two letters
'reduced' cuts number down to its abbreviation NO

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation of number

annotation.surface: A capital city that includes a lowered figure among its welcomes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' wants to be money or a capital letter; it is a capital city.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is one capital city, that of Vietnam.

entries.clue: Change circumscribing degree repeatedly in university, say (4,5)

indicators.note: ALTER draws a line round MA MA
the degree MA is used twice

annotation.surface: Rules on repeated degrees are changing at a university.
annotation.walkthrough: Alma mater is Latin for 'nourishing mother', the old name for the place that educated you.
annotation.definitionFit: One's alma mater is the school or university one attended; 'say' shows a university is one example.

entries.clue: Recipient of gold possibly reconstituted metal lids (9)

indicators.note: the letters are put back together in a new arrangement

annotation.surface: Gold is recast from old metal lids.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gold' looks like the metal being recycled; it is a gold medal, and 'possibly' allows silver or bronze too.
annotation.definitionFit: A medallist is someone awarded a medal, gold for instance.

entries.clue: Sailing vessel caught a sailor tangling with a man at regular intervals (9)

indicators.note: TAR and A MAN are woven together
the two strands alternate, a pair of letters from one then the other

annotation.surface: A boat was caught when a seaman got into a fight with another man now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: TAR and A MAN interleave as T-AM-A-R-AN rather than simply joining.
annotation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled sailing boat.

entries.clue: Abode briefly had severe blow (5)

indicators.note: had is shortened to the contraction 'd

blocks.note: 'd, short for had, as in I'd
a welt is a heavy blow, or the weal it leaves

annotation.surface: A short account of a house that took a heavy hit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abode' looks like a noun, a home; it is the past tense of abide, meaning lived.
annotation.definitionFit: Abode and dwelt are both past tenses meaning lived or stayed.

entries.clue: In extraordinary way, like friend embracing male? Correction, males (12)

indicators.note: PAL wraps its arms round HE NO MEN

blocks.note: -ly is the suffix meaning in the manner of, like

annotation.surface: Someone corrects themselves mid-sentence: a friend hugging a man, no, men.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is someone correcting themselves mid-sentence, and the wordplay takes that literally, keeping the slip, the 'no' and the fix.
annotation.definitionFit: Phenomenally means extraordinarily, in a remarkable way.

entries.clue: Contents of folders delivered earlier (5)

indicators.note: the answer is inside the word folders

blocks.note: the answer sits inside this word, between its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Files in folders were handed over some time ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' means born: someone delivered earlier is older.
annotation.definitionFit: A person born earlier than another is older.

entries.clue: Render senseless conclusions in erroneous report you return (4)

indicators.note: take the last letter of each following word

annotation.surface: Nonsensical conclusions in a false report that you send back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like a reversal instruction; it only supplies its own last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to knock someone out, leave them dazed.

entries.clue: Diagram showing family targeted in odd places (4)

indicators.note: take the letters in the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th positions

annotation.surface: A chart that shows a family being singled out in strange locations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd places' reads as strange locations; it means the odd-numbered letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the branching chart of descent that genealogists draw.

entries.clue: Selected for team in okay position to play (6)

blocks.note: picked for the team = on (the) side
in football or rugby, a player in a legal position, level with or behind the ball, may play

annotation.surface: A player picked for the team is in a legal position.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, ON SIDE, for the first meaning and as one for the second.
annotation.definitionFit: A player who is onside may legally play the ball.

entries.clue: One at home in church (8)

indicators.note: one, I, goes inside MINSTER

blocks.note: a minster is a large church

annotation.surface: Someone who feels at home in church.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay too: I goes in MINSTER, and a minister is indeed one at home in church. 'At home' is the surface's padding for 'in'.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: the whole clue reads straight, since a member of the clergy is indeed at home in a church.

entries.clue: Something felt on head he removed from forehead, oddly (6)

indicators.note: HE is taken out of FOREHEAD
the remaining letters are arranged oddly

annotation.surface: Someone felt something on their head once he'd been taken off their brow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Felt' is the fabric, not the past tense of feel: a fedora is a felt hat. 'Oddly' looks like an odd-letters instruction; here it signals the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat worn on the head.

entries.clue: Recollected ancients, for example (8)

indicators.note: the letters are collected again in a new order

annotation.surface: Elderly people remembered, for example.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, which suits the ancients; split it as re-collected, gathered again.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a case or example.
